commentary_title: VLGC rates normalises amid easing Panama congestion and rising vessel availability
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan routes declined by 7% and 5% WoW, respectively, as increased vessel availability reversed the prior bullish trend. | Easing Panama Canal congestion is resulting in increased VLGC transits, increasing vessel availability. | Low Asian delivered prices and narrowing US-Asia arbitrage also pressurise spot rates. | Meanwhile, Drewry's laden tonnage at anchor in China indicator rose, signalling LPG import recovery amid rising PDH demand. | Other factors—reduced war risk premium and 90-day extension of US- China tariff pause—has reasserted supply-demand fundamentals and led to downward movement in rates.
